memory_update.text: AMSC should be carried forward as the highest-priority U.S.-listed underfollowed candidate for reactive power compensation and grid-stability equipment; key verification is whether Grid segment backlog/revenue is materially tied to utility transmission and renewable interconnection demand.

PLPC should be carried forward as a second-order transmission hardware candidate rather than a direct HVDC/reactive-compensation supplier; it may be useful for grid buildout hardware exposure and underfollowed small/mid-cap screening.

GEV is the reference benchmark for direct HVDC, FACTS, STATCOM and high-voltage capacitor/reactor solutions; use it to identify component chokepoints and possible supplier dependencies, not as the main underfollowed target.
Need a separate non-U.S. listing pass for Quality Power Electrical Equipments, Hammond Power Solutions and other India/Canada/Europe suppliers; this pass was constrained to U.S.-listed companies.
Need filings-level market-cap and liquidity verification for all candidates; market-cap buckets here are approximate based on current finance snapshot and should be refreshed in later layers.

AMSC should remain in the underfollowed lane for hvdc_reactive_power_equipment because it has direct US-listed exposure to dynamic reactive-power compensation and grid-stability equipment via D-VAR and related Grid segment products.

PLPC should remain as an underfollowed adjacent transmission-hardware candidate, but not yet as a proven HVDC/reactive-power equipment supplier; later layers must verify project-level linkage to high-voltage transmission or HVDC corridors.

Hubbell is a diversified reference name for bushings, arresters, insulators, connectors and capacitor-bank / power-factor-correction equipment; it is not a pure underfollowed candidate but helps define the investable product map.

No clean US-listed small-cap pure play was found for HVDC reactors, CTC magnet wire, or high-voltage bushings; likely investable exposure may sit inside foreign-listed suppliers, private manufacturers, or diversified OEMs.

PLPC should be tracked as an underfollowed US-listed transmission-hardware candidate for grid expansion, but its direct tie to HVDC/reactive-power equipment remains unproven and needs product/customer verification.
AMSC is the cleanest US-listed small-cap candidate found for dynamic reactive-power compensation and voltage-control systems through D-VAR/STATCOM-type grid-stability products.

POWL is a second-order electrical infrastructure candidate, more tied to engineered switchgear and power-control systems than to HVDC reactors or capacitors directly; keep but require backlog/end-market proof.

HUBB is a useful reference benchmark for public utility T&D component exposure, including bushings, arresters, insulators, connectors, switches and grid controls, but it is not the underfollowed lane target.

The most node-pure names for HVDC reactors, CTC magnet wire, high-voltage reactive-power compensation and power-quality equipment may be non-US-listed or private; US-listed exposure appears more indirect and requires follow-up on product-level revenue.

Add PLPC as an underfollowed second-order transmission-hardware candidate for the HVDC/reactive-power equipment node; classification should remain hypothesis until filings confirm utility transmission revenue mix, backlog sensitivity, approvals, and margin quality.

Add AMSC as a direct small-cap grid-stability/reactive-compensation candidate via D-VAR/STATCOM and voltage-support products; later layers must isolate grid revenue, backlog, and customer concentration.

Add VSH as an underfollowed passive-components candidate with documented HVDC/STATCOM capacitor applications; materiality is unproven and should be treated as hypothesis until revenue exposure and customer qualifications are verified.
HUBB should be retained as a reference benchmark for utility T&D/substation component demand, not as the main underfollowed alpha candidate.

US-listed universe appears thin for pure-play HVDC reactors, high-voltage bushings, magnet wire, and reactive-power capacitor banks; many direct suppliers are private, foreign-listed, or embedded inside diversified OEMs.

PLPC is less directly tied to HVDC/reactive compensation but is a highly relevant second-order transmission hardware beneficiary. This Layer 1B pass expands the US-listed universe around high-voltage grid-stability equipment. The cleanest US-listed direct exposure found is AMSC through D-VAR and other grid reactive-power / power-quality systems. PLPC is an underfollowed adjacent transmission-hardware supplier with strong relevance to high-voltage grid buildout but weaker direct evidence for HVDC/reactive-power equipment specifically. Hubbell and GE Vernova are included as reference anchors: Hubbell has utility T&D components including bushings, arresters, insulators, connectors and capacitor-bank / power-factor-correction products; GE Vernova is a mega-cap grid OEM with explicit high-voltage capacitor and HVDC/FACTS reactive-power exposure.
